title: Curved Morphs, Breakout Lanes, Difference Type & Snap Sheets
description: Interpolable shape() clip paths, a named-lane breakout grid, mix-blend-mode editorial type, a hold-to-confirm ring and a native dialog bottom sheet.

drops.title: Shape Shifter
drops.description: Four cards morphing between blob, star, petal and gem through clip-path: shape() — real curve commands, interpolated by CSS.
drops.concept: path() was never animatable, so curved clip-path morphs meant SVG or JS. shape() changed that: it takes SVG-style commands in CSS units and interpolates, as long as both states share an identical command list. This drop generates every shape from one radius profile so the command lists always match, and exposes bulge, point count, duration and easing so you can feel where interpolation breaks down.
drops.source: MDN Web Docs — CSS shape() function reference

interaction.mouse: Hover a card to morph it to the next shape in the cycle.
interaction.click: Click to step a card through blob → star → petal → gem.
interaction.touch: Tap a card to morph it; the panel toggle opens the tuning controls.

drops.title: Bleed Control
drops.description: One grid, four named lanes — content, popout, feature, full — and a full-bleed that measures the container instead of the viewport.
drops.concept: The breakout grid names its column lines in pairs, so a block only has to say grid-column: feature to widen; no wrappers and no negative margins. The usual failure is full-bleed itself: 100vw counts the scrollbar and ignores any container, so this drop puts a 100vw bar and a 100cqi bar in the same box and prints how far each one misses by as you squeeze the container.

interaction.mouse: Hover a block to see its lane outline; tune the measure and edge gap in the panel.
interaction.click: Click any block to push it out one lane — content → popout → feature → full.
interaction.touch: Tap blocks to change lanes; tap Squeeze the container to watch the 100vw bar overflow.

drops.title: Difference Type
drops.description: White headlines blended into a moving backdrop with mix-blend-mode: difference, plus a cursor lens that inverts whatever it crosses.
drops.concept: Difference blending subtracts the darker colour from the lighter one, so white type inverts everything under it and black changes nothing at all. That single rule carries the whole editorial look here: three panels of type over moving bars, colour orbs and a gradient grid, and an inverting lens that is nothing more than a white circle set to difference.
drops.source: LogRocket — Creative text styling with the CSS mix-blend-mode property

interaction.mouse: Move the cursor — the lens inverts the type and the backdrop beneath it.
interaction.click: Press anywhere to snap the lens to that point.
interaction.touch: Drag across a panel to move the lens; blend mode and lens size are in the panel.

drops.title: Hold to Confirm
drops.description: Three press-and-hold controls sharing one conic-gradient progress ring — release early and the fill rewinds instead of firing.
drops.concept: Hold-to-confirm replaces a confirmation dialog with a gesture: intent lives in the sustained press, and letting go is the cancel. A conic-gradient ring masked to the border shows progress on any shape — a rectangle, a pill or an orb — and each control captures its pointer so a drag off the button still counts, while pointercancel aborts cleanly.
drops.source: Piotr Działowski — Implementing hold to confirm button

interaction.mouse: Press and hold a control; release early to watch it rewind.
interaction.click: A tap alone does nothing — the gesture is the confirmation.
interaction.touch: Hold with a finger; a completed hold fires a short haptic tick where supported.

drops.title: Snap Sheet
drops.description: A bottom sheet that is still a native <dialog> — focus trap, Esc and ::backdrop free — with drag, snap points and velocity dismissal.
drops.concept: Most bottom sheets rebuild modality from scratch and lose the focus trap along the way. Keeping the sheet a real <dialog> means showModal() supplies the trap, Esc, page inertness and a styleable ::backdrop, leaving only the gesture to write: pointer drag with an upward rubber band, half and full snap points, flick-to-dismiss by velocity, and a scroll-aware policy so dragging only starts when the content is already at the top.
drops.source: viliket — Native-like bottom sheets on the web: the power of modern CSS
tech: Pointer Events drag with velocity tracking

interaction.mouse: Open a sheet, drag its grip, or use the half/full snap buttons.
interaction.click: Pick an action to close the sheet; click the backdrop or press Esc to dismiss.
interaction.touch: Drag the grip and flick down to dismiss; the long list scrolls before it drags.
